redis.name: redis
redis.title: Valkey cache
redis.summary: A managed Valkey cache with Sentinel failover, on spotahome/redis-operator. Valkey rather than Redis, per ADR-011; every Redis client works against it.

create.name: create
create.summary: Create or replace a Valkey cache.

flags.name: --class
flags.summary: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.

flags.name: --cluster-id
flags.summary: The cluster whose namespace holds the RedisFailover.

flags.name: --cpu
flags.summary: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

flags.name: --enabled
flags.summary: Whether the operator runs a metrics exporter beside every Valkey and every Sentinel pod.

flags.name: --fsync
flags.summary: How often the append-only file reaches the disk. Read only when the mode is AOF; everysec can lose the last second of writes.

flags.name: --location
flags.summary: The region the cache is billed in.

flags.name: --maxmemory-policy
flags.summary: What happens when the cache reaches its memory limit. noeviction returns an error to the writer rather than dropping a key somebody is relying on.

flags.name: --memory
flags.summary: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset. It also sets maxmemory, so a cache evicts or refuses before the kernel kills the pod.

flags.name: --mode
flags.summary: Replication topology. Sentinel is the only one this operator implements, and a client written against it is not portable to a sharded deployment, so it may not change after create.

flags.name: --name
flags.summary: The resource's name within its group.

flags.name: --persistence-mode
flags.summary: None keeps nothing, RDB snapshots periodically, AOF appends every write.

flags.name: --preset
flags.summary: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Caches use the m1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 8 GiB.

flags.name: --replicas
flags.summary: Number of Valkey instances, including the primary. One is a single point of failure and is offered for development only.

flags.name: --resource-group
flags.summary: The resource group. docs/plan/06 § The hierarchy.

flags.name: --size
flags.summary: Persistent volume size in Kubernetes quantity form. Unused when the mode is None, which keeps the data directory in memory.

flags.name: --subscription
flags.summary: The subscription. Defaults to the current profile.

flags.name: --tags
flags.summary: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

kafka-clusters.name: kafka-clusters
kafka-clusters.title: Kafka cluster
kafka-clusters.summary: A managed Apache Kafka cluster on Strimzi in KRaft mode, with Cruise Control, configurable retention and an optional firewalled external listener.

create.name: create
create.summary: Create or replace a Kafka cluster.

flags.name: --allowed-cidrs
flags.summary: Source ranges permitted to reach the external listener. Required in substance rather than in schema: an empty list with external exposure on renders a load balancer that accepts nothing, which is the safe reading of an unfinished configuration.

flags.name: --class
flags.summary: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.

flags.name: --cluster-id
flags.summary: The cluster whose namespace holds the Strimzi objects.

flags.name: --cpu
flags.summary: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

flags.name: --cruise-control-enabled
flags.summary: Whether Cruise Control runs. On by default: docs/plan/12 puts it in the chart rather than in a follow-up, because rebalancing a Kafka cluster by hand is the operational cost that makes this the most demanding service in the catalogue.

flags.name: --delete-claim
flags.summary: Whether deleting the resource also deletes the log volumes. Off by default, so a mistaken delete leaves the data recoverable by hand.

flags.name: --external-enabled
flags.summary: Whether the cluster is reachable from outside the Kubernetes cluster. Off by default — docs/plan/12 § Cross-cutting decisions makes external exposure never the default, because a managed broker on a public IP with a weak password is the most common cloud breach there is.

flags.name: --hours
flags.summary: Default retention in hours. A week by default.

flags.name: --location
flags.summary: The region the cluster is billed in.

flags.name: --memory
flags.summary: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

flags.name: --min-in-sync-replicas
flags.summary: How many replicas must acknowledge a write before it is committed. Must be below the replication factor, or the cluster cannot tolerate one broker restart.

flags.name: --monitoring-enabled
flags.summary: Whether the operator runs a Kafka Exporter alongside the cluster, exposing consumer-lag and topic metrics to the platform's metrics stack.

flags.name: --name
flags.summary: The resource's name within its group.

flags.name: --nodes
flags.summary: Number of Kafka nodes, each acting as both a KRaft controller and a broker. Use an odd number: a quorum of two tolerates no failures, and one is a single point of failure offered for development only.

flags.name: --partitions
flags.summary: Default partition count for a new topic.

flags.name: --preset
flags.summary: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Brokers use the c1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 2 GiB and guaranteed rather than burstable.

flags.name: --replication-factor
flags.summary: Default replication factor for a new topic. Must not exceed the node count, or every produce to a new topic fails.

flags.name: --resource-group
flags.summary: The resource group. docs/plan/06 § The hierarchy.

flags.name: --retention-size
flags.summary: Default retention by partition size, in Kubernetes quantity form. Empty means retention is by time alone.

flags.name: --storage-size
flags.summary: Log volume size per node, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

flags.name: --subscription
flags.summary: The subscription. Defaults to the current profile.

flags.name: --tags
flags.summary: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

flags.name: --tenant
flags.summary: The tenant. Defaults to the current profile.

flags.name: --tls
flags.summary: Whether the in-cluster listener requires TLS. On by default; turning it off is a plaintext broker on the pod network.

flags.name: --version
flags.summary: Apache Kafka version. Minor upgrades are applied automatically in the maintenance window; a major upgrade is an explicit update to this field.
